reviewNote: Point-in-time snapshot, NOT an eternal Cloudflare IP contract. Cloudflare may change these addresses at any time and DNS answers rotate. Re-verify this snapshot against current Cloudflare documentation and a fresh resolution of both region hostnames before S5.5-F Production activation and at every later firewall change.

transport.note: cloudflared is pinned to --protocol http2, which uses TCP/7844 only. Cloudflare documents TCP and UDP on 7844; S5.5 deliberately allows TCP only and never opens QUIC.

excluded.reason: QUIC transport is not used; --protocol http2 is pinned, so UDP/7844 stays denied
the connector needs no outbound HTTPS; TCP/443 stays denied
no broad Internet egress; only the reviewed /32 endpoints are reachable
broad published Cloudflare ranges are not used; only exact tunnel endpoints
no DNS exception in S5.5-D; the Production resolver path must be measured before S5.5-F

sources.detail: Cloudflare One docs, Tunnel with firewall: https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/configure-tunnels/tunnel-with-firewall/ documents port 7844 for region1.v2.argotunnel.com and region2.v2.argotunnel.com and lists these exact IPv4 addresses.

Local read-only A-record resolution of region1.v2.argotunnel.com and region2.v2.argotunnel.com returned exactly these 20 addresses (10 per region), matching the documented list with no extra or missing entry.
Documentation list and live resolution agreed exactly; no address was inferred, guessed, or copied from an earlier plan draft.
